segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna teaches that one may not purchase from him even «deer meat.» The Gemara explains that the reason is «that» it could be «confused with» meat «of a calf,» as they are similar in appearance.

segments.he: וְלֹא עוֹרוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן עֲבוּדִים. הָא עֲבוּדִים זָבְנִינַן. אִם אִיתָא דִּבְכוֹר הֲוָה — לָא הֲוָה טָרַח בֵּיהּ, סָבַר: אִי שָׁמְעוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן מַפְסְדוּ לֵיהּ מִינַּאי.
segments.en: The mishna teaches: «Nor» may one purchase from him «hides that are not tanned.» The Gemara infers from here that «we» may «purchase tanned» hides from one who is suspect with regard to firstborn animals. The reason is that «if it is so that it is» a hide «of a firstborn, he would not make» such «an effort with it» to tan it. This is because he would «think: If the Sages hear that» this hide is from a firstborn, they will «cause me a loss» by confiscating it «from me.»
